commands.summary: Create a song and open it: Mixer 1 "Sources", Mixer 2 "Buses" with the bus "Main" → master, and the output port "Main" (R-MIX-3).
Open a song.
Write the .slp (a path saves it there).
Close the song and return Home.

Write addresses: project.bpm, <strip>.gain, <clip>.at, <device>.<param> (any DSP registry parameter, in its unit), … — `api` lists every one. An unknown address or parameter is refused. A value starting with `=` is a FORMULA that drives a number (R-AUTO); a plain number clears it.
Print an address's stored value.

Undo the last edit (prints what). Consecutive `set`s of the same addresses — a fader dragged — are ONE step. A machine setting, the transport and a save are not edits; a new or opened song starts a new history.
Redo what `undo` took back; a new edit clears it.
Add a mixer page after the last one.
Delete an empty mixer. Refused while strips live on it.
Move a mixer to position <index> (0 = first). Refused if it would make any route point backward.

Add a strip. Default mixer: the first for audio/instrument, the second for a bus; default output: "Main" — the bus that leaves the nearest later mixer with buses, else the one leaving its own mixer (the new strip is then placed BEFORE it, so the route goes forward), else master. An instrument strip gets its instrument (default synth) as its first device; --sample <file> gives a sampler its sound (R-EDM-8).
Delete a strip and its rack. Refused while clips play through it or strips route to it, unless --with-clips (its clips go too).

Move a strip to another mixer (at its end) and/or to position --order <n> on it (0 = first); its mixer's strips renumber in their new order, as `mixer move` renumbers mixers. Refused if a route would point backward.
Move EVERY clip playing through <ch> to strip --to, one edit. Refused across kinds: audio clips need an audio strip, note clips an instrument strip; a bus plays no clips.
Set a strip's main output: a strip LATER in processing order (a later mixer, or after it on its own), master, or an output port.

Add a send (post-fader unless --pre). Same forward-only rule as `route`. With --sidechain it is a KEY: it feeds the target's compressors' detectors (their Sidechain switch), not its input, and goes to a strip (R-MIX-15).
Remove a send.
Insert a DSP registry device into a rack (default: at the end). An instrument goes only first on an instrument strip.
Remove a device from its rack. An instrument strip keeps its instrument.
Move a device within its rack.
Add a timeline lane at the bottom. With --strip <instrument>: that instrument's TRACK — what is put on it plays through it, and it shows the strip's name until given its own (R-LANE-3).
Delete a lane. Refused while clips are drawn on it, unless --with-clips.
Move a lane to row <index> (0 = the top); the lanes renumber in their new order.

Place a clip. With --src: an audio clip; a file the song has not used gets its own new strip on the first mixer (R-MIX-2), a used one reuses its strip. With --strip <instrument>: a note clip of --pattern (a new empty 4-beat pattern if none). With --instrument <type>: the same on a NEW instrument strip of that type — what dropping an instrument does (R-BROWSE-3). With no --lane it goes on the lane its strip's clips are on (the newest one's), a new lane only for a strip with none; --lane new asks for a new one (R-SVC-8). On an instrument's TRACK (--lane <ln>) a note clip plays through that instrument — --strip may be left out, --pattern places that pattern; audio and --instrument are refused there (R-LANE-3). Prints the clip, then `made:` and whatever else it made.

Move a clip in time, to another lane (where it is drawn), and/or another strip (what it sounds through). Onto an instrument's TRACK a note clip is re-routed to that instrument (and says so); a clip on a track told --strip <another> goes to that one's track; audio is refused on a track (R-LANE-3).
A copy right after it (or at --at); --count N makes N copies end to end. A note clip's copy plays the SAME pattern — linked. Prints the first copy, then `made:` the rest.
Give a note clip its own copy of its pattern.
Remove a clip.
Create an empty pattern.

Add a note to a pattern — every clip of it changes. A pitch is a number, a name (C4 = 60, F#3, Bb2) or a kit's pad (kick). --chord <Cm7> adds a chord instead (its root in --octave, default 4; --inversion n raises its n lowest notes an octave) as ONE edit — the qualities are under Notation.
Remove the note at that pitch and time.
Change the note at --pitch / --at: move it (--to-pitch, --to-at), resize it (--length), set its velocity (--vel) — one gesture, one line. Refused onto another note.
Move every note's start onto the grid (default a sixteenth, 0.25), delaying every second grid step by --swing of a step. Notes that land on one another merge (the louder stays).

Many notes in ONE edit (one undo step): each <note> is <pitch>@<beat>[:<length>[:<vel>]] — C4@0:0.5:90, kick@1, E4@2::70. --length / --vel are the defaults (0.25, 100). A bad token is refused by name and nothing lands. Prints how many; warns of notes past the pattern's end.

A step row: x = a note, X = an accent (velocity 127), . or - = a rest, one per --step (default 0.25) from --at (default 0); spaces and | are ignored. REPLACES that pitch's notes in the span; --length defaults to a step. One edit.
A new pattern with the same notes and length (named "<name> copy"). Prints its id.
Remove every note (or only --pitch's).
Delete a pattern. Refused while a clip plays it (naming the clips).
Move every note by --semi semitones (negative = down). Refused if a note would leave 0–127.
Its notes, one per line in the `notes add` notation (pitch as a name or pad), the number after `#`.

Automate a number: a new automation named "<owner> · <parameter>", ranged as it, holding its value from beat 0 to the song's end, shown on the timeline — and the address bound to `=au_n`. Prints the id.
An automation from nothing (default range 0…1). It moves nothing until a formula reads it. Prints the id.
Delete an automation. Refused while a formula reads it, unless --unbind (those bindings are cleared).
Add a point (one at the same beat is replaced). Its shape governs the segment after it (a bezier point's handles start flat: speed 0, influence 33.333 %).
Move the point at --at to another beat and/or value.
Remove the point at --at.

Set how the curve leaves the point at --at. A BEZIER point is Interstellar's key (R-ANIM-2): on each side a speed — the slope there, in the automation's unit per beat — and an influence, how far into the neighbouring segment it pulls (0 < x ≤ 100 %); flags not given are kept. One line per handle gesture.
Clear an address's formula: it plays its own stored value again. (`set <address>=<number>` clears and sets.)
The value an address plays at a beat (default 0); --explain shows its formula and every name it reads.

Render offline: the master to --out; with --stems, each named strip's (`all`: every strip's) post-fader output to <out>.<ch>.wav; with --ports, each output port to <out>.<port>.wav. The tail runs until −90 dBFS or 10 s. Every file starts at --from exactly: the latency of a lookahead device (a limiter) is compensated and trimmed (R-MIX-17).
Every route and send at once: rows = strips, columns = destinations.
The mix report: unused strips, clips on muted strips, unreachable strips, single-input buses, offline media, unknown devices, clipping.

The whole AppModel; --stable omits what changes with time. --json --compact: the SONG only (no registry, machine, recents or browser), on one line; a device lists only its non-default parameters as `name=value`, a pattern its notes in the `notes add` notation.
The song as a tree of ids and names: mixers → strips (kind, devices, output, sends), the master, lanes → clips (at, length, pattern or file), patterns (length, notes, clips), automations.
One node's fields that differ from their defaults; a device's non-default parameters with their units (and the default); `show project` for the song.
This document: every command, event, model field and device parameter.

The MACHINE's settings (never a song's): sampleRate (new songs, and the clock device's rate), bufferSize (frames), output / input (device ids from `devices list`; empty = the system default), port.<name>=<device>:<channel> (where a song's port plays on this machine), metronome (on|off), metronomeLevel (dB), auditionLevel (dB, the browser's preview), newBpm / newSig (what a new song starts at), reducedMotion (on|off), showIds (on|off: every object's id beside its name, R-UI-11). Saved at once.
The machine's settings.
Add a sample folder to the browser's quick-access list.
Remove a sample folder from the list (the folder itself is untouched).
Reorder the sample folders.
List this machine's audio devices (ids for `settings set output=…`).
List a folder for the browser: sub-folders, audio files, songs.
Take a song off Home's recent list (the file is untouched).

Play on the clock device (settings output), from --from or where the transport stands. Edits while playing are heard: a gain, a pan, a mute, a solo, a device parameter at once; anything structural by a new engine swapped in at the same position.
Stop; the transport stays where it was heard.
Move the transport (playing or not).
Loop between two beats while playing; `off` ends it.
Hear a sample now, outside the song (the browser's preview): through the output device at the audition level, to its end; `stop` ends it. Not an edit, never in a render.
Let time pass (playback goes on, the model's transport and meters update) — for scripts that listen.

events.name: info
events.summary: A note worth logging; carries no state.

events.name: error
events.summary: Something failed. Also set as AppModel.lastError.

events.name: command.rejected
events.summary: A line was refused (R-SVC-3): unknown verb, flag, address or parameter; a refused edit.

events.name: project.changed
events.summary: A node was added, removed, moved or re-routed. what = e.g. strip.added, clip.moved, route.set. Every node a command makes is announced, one event each (R-SVC-8).

events.name: params.changed
events.summary: An address was written; value is what was STORED, canonical (a value out of range is refused, never clamped — R-SVC-8).

events.name: render.finished
events.summary: A render was written; peak is the master's, dBFS.

events.name: render.failed
events.summary: A render stopped with an error.

events.name: settings.changed
events.summary: A machine setting changed and was saved: sampleRate, bufferSize, output, input, port.<name>, folders.

events.name: browse.changed
events.summary: The browser now lists this folder.

events.name: transport.changed
events.summary: Play, stop, seek or loop: playing 1/0, position in beats, loop `from-to` or `off`.

events.name: audition.changed
events.summary: A sample previewed from the browser started (playing 1) or ended — stopped, or to its end (playing 0).

master, a strip id, or a port id (resolved)
the formula driving the gain, "" = none (R-AUTO-1)
the formula driving the pan, "" = none
false when muted or silenced by another strip's solo (R-MIX-7)
an index into the track colours: its own, else from its id — never −1
a strip on a later mixer, master, or a port
the formula driving the send's gain, "" = none
a sidechain key: into the target's compressors' detectors, not its input (R-MIX-15)
the rack, in order (an instrument strip's first is its instrument)
it plays a recorded sound (a sampler, R-EDM-8)
that sound, as stored (relative to the song); "" = none
false when this build's registry lacks the type (kept, not played)
the parameter last written, by anyone (R-WIN-2)
every registry parameter, stored or default (R-UI-5)
Hz, dB, ms, st, ct, oct, or empty
as stored: a number, or a choice's name
engineering units; a choice = its index
a control's taper: moves in ratios (frequencies, times)
the formula driving it, "" = its own value plays (R-AUTO-1)
the last played block's peaks, L/R (R-PLAY-3)
fed by: clips playing through it (R-MIX-8)
fed by: the lanes those clips are drawn on
fed by: strips whose output or a send lands here
where its output or a send may go (R-MIX-4): strips LATER in processing order (a later mixer, or after it on its own), master, output ports
where a sidechain key may go (R-MIX-15): the strips of targets
the master's rack, shaped like strips[].devices
R-LANE-3: the instrument strip it is the track of — what is on it plays through it; empty = a plain lane
false: a track showing its instrument strip's name (renaming the strip renames it)
the lane it is drawn on ("" = its strip's own row)
the file could not be read
clips playing the same pattern, this one included (R-CLIP-3)
the strip its first clip plays through
that strip's instrument type (what names its keys)
the address it was made from (a hint, not a link)
linear | hold | smooth | bezier — the segment after it (bezier: both its sides)
bezier (R-AUTO-10): the slope arriving, in the automation's unit per beat
bezier: how far into the segment before it that slope pulls, % (0 < x ≤ 100)
bezier: the slope leaving, unit per beat
bezier: how far into the segment after it, %
its value at the playhead (`transport.position`) by the engine's own evaluator; follows the transport while playing (R-AUTO-11)
the automations and addresses it reads
false = INERT: the address's own value plays
its value at the HEARD position (R-MIX-16): the engine's while playing, eval's at the transport when stopped
the routing matrix (R-MIX-9), computed once for every face
its columns: every strip some strip may or does reach (processing order), "master", the output ports — every route and key has a cell
the file is gone or no longer a song
new songs, and the clock device's rate
what that buffer costs at that rate
the clock device ('' = the system default)
the browser's quick-access folders, in order
clicks while playing (R-TIME-4), never in a render
dB: a sample previewed from the browser (R-EDM-9)
the UI's tweens collapse (with the OS's own setting)
every object's id drawn beside its name (R-UI-11)
beats; equal to loopFrom = no loop
the clock device ('' = the system default)
L/R peaks of the last played block
a sample heard from the browser, outside the song (R-EDM-9)
0 … 1 of the file handed to the device
the DSP registry: every instrument and effect a strip can host (R-BROWSE-1)
the registry type, what `device add --type` and `--instrument` take
it plays a recorded sound: give it one with --sample / <dv>.sample (R-EDM-8)

devices.label: Basic Synth
devices.summary: Two oscillators and noise through a resonant filter and an amplitude envelope; 16 voices.

devices.label: Drum Machine
devices.summary: Ten synthesized pads on the GM drum notes (36 kick … 56 cowbell); the closed hat chokes the open hat.

devices.label: Sampler
devices.summary: Plays a recorded sound: pitched by the note (chromatic) or as recorded (one-shot); a span, reverse, an ADSR.

devices.label: Compressor
devices.summary: Feed-forward peak compressor; with Sidechain on it listens to another track (its key).

devices.label: EQ
devices.summary: Low cut, low shelf, three peaks, high shelf, high cut.

devices.label: Drive
devices.summary: tanh waveshaper with a tone low-pass.

devices.label: Filter
devices.summary: The synth's resonant state-variable filter, with a dry/wet mix.

devices.label: Limiter
devices.summary: Brickwall lookahead limiter: the output never exceeds the ceiling.

notation.pitch: a number 0-127, a name (C4 = 60, F#3, Bb2, c-1 = 0) or a kit's pad (kick)
notation.steps: x = a note, X = an accent (127), . or - = a rest; spaces and | ignored
